intent.raw_query: Greece under $2000, beaches and local food, summer 2026, flying from NYC

experiences.name: Navagio Beach (Shipwreck Beach) Visit
experiences.description: Take a boat tour to the iconic Navagio Beach on Zakynthos, one of Greece's most photographed beaches. The stunning turquoise waters, white sand, and the famous shipwreck make this an unmissable experience. Boat tours depart regularly from Porto Vromi or Zakynthos Town.

experiences.name: Athens Central Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the vibrant Varvakios Agora (Athens Central Market) and surrounding streets in Monastiraki. Sample local cheeses, olives, cured meats, fresh seafood, and traditional Greek street food like souvlaki and spanakopita. Engage with local vendors and discover authentic Greek flavors.

experiences.name: Elafonissi Pink Sand Beach Day
experiences.description: Visit the breathtaking Elafonissi Beach, famous for its unique pinkish sand created by crushed shells and coral. Wade through shallow crystal-clear lagoons and snorkel in the warm Mediterranean waters. The beach is part of a protected nature reserve and is one of Crete's most beautiful natural wonders.

experiences.name: Traditional Cretan Cooking Class
experiences.description: Join a hands-on cooking class in a local Cretan home or taverna and learn to prepare traditional dishes such as dakos (barley rusk salad), lamb with stamnagathi (wild greens), and loukoumades (honey fritters). Includes a visit to a local market to source fresh ingredients and a full meal with local wine.

experiences.name: Sunset Sailing & Seafood Experience in Santorini
experiences.description: Board a traditional Greek catamaran for a sunset sailing cruise around the volcanic caldera of Santorini. Swim in hot springs, snorkel in clear Aegean waters, and enjoy a freshly prepared onboard BBQ featuring grilled octopus, shrimp, and local mezedes paired with Greek wine as the sun sets over Oia.

weather.summary: Hot and sunny. Sea warm enough for swimming.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Greece
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Arrival day
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - Arrival day
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Athens International Airport at 22:30 on flight UA. Clear customs, collect luggage, and take the X95 express bus or Metro Line 3 to central Athens to connect to your transfer toward Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and get settled into your beachfront room.

meals.breakfast: N/A
meals.lunch: N/A
meals.dinner: Grab a quick gyro or souvlaki wrap from a late-night street kiosk near the airport or transit hub (budget €3–5). Many Greek kiosks stay open past midnight.

day_by_day.notes: Keep arrival night simple. Pre-book your airport transfer or use public transport (Metro + bus combo ~€9) to save money. Have some euros ready for small purchases. Rest well — the adventure begins tomorrow!

day_by_day.morning: Wake up and take your first walk along the beachfront outside Aegean Bliss Resort. Enjoy the warm morning sun and dip your feet in the clear Aegean Sea. Explore the immediate shoreline, take photos, and get oriented with the local area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the nearest local village or town on foot or by local bus. Browse the main market street, visit a small Orthodox church, and pick up a detailed map from the local tourist info point. Swim at the public beach section near the resort — sea temperatures are perfect at this time of year.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the waterfront promenade as the sun sets. Find a taverna with plastic chairs and checkered tablecloths — a sure sign of authentic, affordable Greek food.

meals.breakfast: Enjoy a simple Greek breakfast at the resort or a nearby bakery — spanakopita (spinach pie) and a freddo espresso (budget €3–5).
meals.lunch: Grab a fresh cheese pie (tiropita) and a cold Mythos beer from a local periptero (kiosk) on the beach (budget €4–6).
meals.dinner: Dinner at a family-run taverna: order grilled octopus, Greek salad, and house wine. Ask for the daily special (mageirefta) for the best value (budget €10–14 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Exchange or withdraw euros from an ATM today if needed. Avoid airport exchange booths. Local buses are typically €1.50–2.50 per ride. Stay hydrated — it's hot at 29°C!

day_by_day.morning: Early morning swim at the beachfront before the crowds arrive — the sea is warm and calm in the mornings. Spend time snorkeling if you have gear (cheap rental sets available locally for ~€5/day).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby archaeological site or ancient ruins accessible by local bus. Greece is dotted with free or low-cost historical sites even in beach resort areas. Bring water and a hat — midday heat is intense.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area and join locals for the traditional Greek 'volta' — an evening stroll along the waterfront. Window shop, people-watch, and enjoy the cooler evening air.

meals.breakfast: Greek yogurt with honey and walnuts from a local dairy shop or supermarket — a cheap and filling start (budget €2–3).
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic from the local supermarket: olives, feta, crusty bread, tomatoes, and bottled water (budget €5–7).
meals.dinner: Try a psistaria (grill house) for souvlaki platters with pita, tzatziki, and chips. Filling and delicious (budget €8–12 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Sunscreen is essential — UV index is very high in June. Buy it locally but note it can be pricier than back home; bring some from home if possible.

day_by_day.morning: Take a local bus or shared taxi to a quieter, less-touristy beach a short distance from the resort. Secluded coves and crystal-clear water are often just a short ride away. Arrive early to claim a good spot.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon swimming, sunbathing, and relaxing on the quieter beach. Look for sea urchins and small fish in the shallows — the water is incredibly clear. Walk along any coastal paths nearby.
day_by_day.evening: Head back to the resort area. Visit a local ouzeri (ouzo bar) for a traditional aperitif experience — a small ouzo is often served with free meze snacks.

meals.breakfast: Toast with local honey and a Greek coffee (ellinikos kafes) at a neighborhood kafeneio (coffee house) — very cheap and very Greek (budget €2–4).
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood at a small beachside shack — grilled sardines or fried calamari with lemon and bread (budget €8–10).
meals.dinner: Mezedes (small sharing plates) at an ouzeri: dolmades, taramosalata, grilled halloumi, and bread. Order several dishes to share for variety and value (budget €10–13 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Ask locals or hotel staff for their favorite hidden beach — they always know the best spots tourists miss. Bring cash to smaller beach establishments as card machines are rare.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the local open-air laiki agora (farmers' market) — these typically run on set weekdays and are a fantastic way to experience Greek daily life. Buy fresh fruit, local cheese, honey, and olives directly from producers at very low prices.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cook or assemble a DIY lunch with your market finds at the resort. Spend the afternoon at the resort beach, reading, swimming, and relaxing. This is a great low-cost, low-energy afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the local neighborhood on foot after 6pm when the heat subsides. Discover small chapels, colorful bougainvillea-draped houses, and hidden courtyards. End the evening with an ice cream from a local gelateria.

meals.breakfast: Fresh pastries and coffee from the market or a local bakery (budget €3–4).
meals.lunch: DIY market picnic — assembled from your morning market haul. Eat at the beach or a shaded park (budget €5–7 total for market shopping).
meals.dinner: Find a restaurant offering a set menu or tourist menu deal — often 2–3 courses including a drink for €12–15. Look for chalkboard signs outside tavernas.

day_by_day.notes: Greek markets are usually morning-only (7am–2pm). Check with hotel staff for the local market day and location. Bring a reusable bag.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip by local ferry or bus to a nearby island or coastal town. Greece's ferry network is extensive and affordable for short hops. Enjoy the sea crossing and the views of the Aegean.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the day-trip destination — walk the main town, visit the port, browse local shops, and find a beach for an afternoon swim. Many smaller islands have stunning beaches with almost no crowds.
day_by_day.evening: Return ferry or bus back to base. Enjoy a relaxed dinner near the resort after a full day of exploration.

meals.breakfast: Quick coffee and koulouri (sesame bread ring) before departure — sold at port kiosks for €1–2.
meals.lunch: Fresh fish lunch at the day-trip destination — order the catch of the day grilled simply with olive oil and lemon (budget €10–14).
meals.dinner: Simple dinner near the resort — a bowl of fasolada (bean soup) or lentil soup with bread at a traditional kafeneio (budget €6–9).

day_by_day.notes: Check ferry schedules in advance and confirm return times. Bring cash, sunscreen, and a light layer for the sea breeze on the ferry. Ferry tickets for short hops typically cost €5–15 each way.

day_by_day.morning: Rest morning — sleep in and enjoy a slow breakfast. Spend the morning at the resort beach. This is the summer solstice — the longest day of the year, meaning extra hours of beautiful daylight to enjoy.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a bicycle or scooter (budget €8–15/day for a bicycle, €20–30 for a scooter) and explore the surrounding coastal roads and villages at your own pace. Stop wherever looks interesting.
day_by_day.evening: Find a hilltop or elevated spot to watch the sunset — on the summer solstice the sun sets late, often after 8:30pm in Greece, making for a spectacular long golden hour.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely breakfast at the resort or a nearby café — scrambled eggs, village bread, local jam, and coffee (budget €4–6).
meals.lunch: Stop at a village taverna during your bike/scooter ride — order whatever the cook recommends that day (budget €8–11).
meals.dinner: Celebrate the solstice with a slightly more indulgent dinner — fresh grilled fish (tsipoura or lavraki) at a seafront taverna with a carafe of local white wine (budget €15–18 per person).

day_by_day.notes: If renting a scooter, ensure you have the appropriate license category. Always wear a helmet. Bicycle rental is the most budget-friendly option and great for shorter distances.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a local monastery or Byzantine church in the region — these are usually free to enter and offer a fascinating glimpse into Greek Orthodox culture and history. Dress modestly (shoulders and knees covered).
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to a beach known for water sports — many Greek resorts offer affordable paddleboarding, kayaking, or pedalo hire. Spend the afternoon on the water (budget €5–15 for 1-hour rental).
day_by_day.evening: Take a cooking class or food tour if available locally — many Greek towns offer affordable 2-hour cooking experiences where you learn to make dishes like moussaka or spanakopita (budget €20–35 if available, optional).

meals.breakfast: Bougatsa (cream-filled phyllo pastry) and coffee from a local bakery — a beloved Greek morning treat (budget €3–5).
meals.lunch: Gyros wrap with pork or chicken, tzatziki, tomato, and onion from a local gyradiko (gyros shop) — one of Greece's best budget meals (budget €3–5).
meals.dinner: Moussaka and a Greek salad at a traditional taverna — a classic combination and very filling (budget €10–13 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Monasteries often have strict visiting hours (typically open 9am–1pm and 5pm–8pm, closed midday). Check locally. Modest dress is required — scarves and wraps are sometimes provided at the entrance.

day_by_day.morning: Spend the morning at a beach with notably clear water — go snorkeling or simply float and enjoy. June water temperatures in Greece are around 23–25°C, ideal for long swims.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local olive grove or vineyard if accessible — many Greek farms welcome visitors informally, and some offer free or very cheap tastings of olive oil and wine. Ask at the hotel for recommendations.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a free local cultural event, outdoor cinema, or village festival if one is happening — June is festival season in Greece with many free open-air events.

meals.breakfast: Horiatiko psomi (village bread) with local olive oil and oregano, plus a coffee — the simplest and most authentic Greek breakfast (budget €2–3).
meals.lunch: Dakos (Cretan bruschetta with tomato, feta, and olives on barley rusk) — light, refreshing, and very cheap at most cafés (budget €4–6).
meals.dinner: Kleftiko (slow-cooked lamb) or stifado (beef stew) at a traditional oven-cooked restaurant — hearty and flavorful (budget €11–15 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Check local event listings on community boards or ask hotel staff about any panigiri (village festivals) happening nearby — these often include free music, dancing, and cheap food stalls.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning hike along a coastal trail if one exists near the resort. Many Greek coastal areas have scenic walking paths with stunning sea views. Start early (7–9am) before the heat peaks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cool off with an afternoon at the beach. Try cliff jumping or exploring sea caves if safely accessible nearby — ask locals for the best spots. Alternatively, find a shaded café and work through a Greek coffee and a good book.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the local port or harbor area in the evening — watch fishing boats return, chat with fishermen, and enjoy the lively atmosphere as locals gather for the evening.

meals.breakfast: Energy-boosting breakfast before the hike: Greek yogurt, granola, fresh fruit, and water from the supermarket (budget €3–5).
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood directly from a harbor-side fish taverna — ask what came in that morning for the freshest and best-priced option (budget €9–13).
meals.dinner: Grilled prawns (garides) and a carafe of ouzo or tsipouro with ice at a harbor taverna as the sun goes down (budget €12–15 per person).

day_by_day.notes: For coastal hikes, always bring at least 1.5 liters of water per person, wear sturdy shoes, and let someone know your route. Trails may not always be well-marked.

day_by_day.morning: Spend a leisurely morning exploring local shops and boutiques — look for handmade ceramics, local honey, herbs, and olive oil as affordable souvenirs. Bargaining is not common in Greece but asking for a small discount is acceptable.
day_by_day.afternoon: Find a secluded beach or a less-visited cove for a private afternoon swim. Pack your own snacks and drinks from the supermarket to keep costs down. Read, relax, and soak up the Greek sun.
day_by_day.evening: Join locals for the evening ritual of coffee and conversation at a seafront kafeneio. Order a frappe (iced Nescafé — the Greek summer staple) and people-watch as the town comes alive after the heat of the day.

meals.breakfast: Tiropita or spanakopita from a local bakery with a coffee — a classic Greek on-the-go breakfast (budget €3–4).
meals.lunch: Supermarket picnic at the beach: pre-made Greek salad containers, olives, pita, hummus, and cold drinks (budget €6–8).
meals.dinner: Psarotaverna (fish taverna) dinner — order fried whitebait (marides), grilled sea bream, and a shared Greek salad with local wine (budget €13–16 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Great souvenir buys in Greece: local thyme honey (€5–10), dried oregano, mountain tea, and small ceramic pieces. Avoid tourist shops near main attractions — the same items are cheaper in local supermarkets and village shops.

day_by_day.morning: Take one final day trip to a nearby attraction you haven't yet visited — a different beach, a hilltop village, or a local museum. Make the most of your last full day of exploration.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort for a long, leisurely final swim in the Aegean. Spend the afternoon reflecting on the trip, journaling, or simply floating in the warm sea.
day_by_day.evening: Splurge slightly on a farewell dinner at one of the better local tavernas — this is your last evening, so enjoy a proper Greek feast with multiple courses and local wine.

meals.breakfast: Full Greek breakfast at a café: eggs, village sausage, feta, olives, tomatoes, and coffee (budget €6–8).
meals.lunch: Light lunch — a creamy tzatziki dip with pita bread and a cold drink at a beach bar (budget €5–7).
meals.dinner: Farewell feast: start with mezedes (taramosalata, dolmades, saganaki), then grilled lamb chops (paidakia) or fresh lobster spaghetti, and finish with a complimentary dessert (many tavernas offer loukoumades or fruit as a gift). Toast with local wine or raki (budget €18–22 per person — your one splurge!).

day_by_day.notes: Pack tonight or early tomorrow morning. Confirm your departure transfer or transport to the airport. Keep some euros aside for airport purchases and tips. Leave a small tip (5–10%) at your favorite taverna as a thank-you.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — wake up for one last sunrise walk on the beach. Take photos, collect a small shell or pebble as a free memento, and say goodbye to the Aegean Sea. Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort and arrange transfer to the airport.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart for Athens International Airport. Allow plenty of time for check-in and security. Browse duty-free for any last-minute Greek products (olive oil, mastiha sweets, or Greek coffee).
day_by_day.evening: Board your return flight home, carrying memories of 13 incredible days in Greece — beaches, food, culture, and sunshine.

meals.breakfast: Final Greek breakfast — a koulouri from a street vendor and a last freddo cappuccino at an airport café or nearby spot (budget €3–5).
meals.lunch: Light airport meal or snacks packed from the supermarket the night before to avoid expensive airport food (budget €5–8 if eating at airport).
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or airport food depending on departure time.

day_by_day.notes: Check out time is typically 11am — confirm with the resort. Keep your travel documents, boarding pass, and passport easily accessible. The Metro Line 3 from central Athens to the airport costs ~€9 and is the most budget-friendly airport transfer option. Allow 2–3 hours before your flight for check-in.

trip_options.title: Classic Greece Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Athens International Airport on flight UA at 22:30. Clear customs, collect luggage, and arrange private transfer or express bus to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and settle into your beachfront room.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in transit
meals.lunch: N/A — in transit
meals.dinner: Grab a light late-night snack at the airport or a 24-hour gyros stand near the hotel upon arrival

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light. Pre-book your airport transfer in advance to avoid delays at night. Confirm hotel check-in arrangements for late arrival. Rest well — big days ahead!

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the resort. Take a slow orientation walk along the beachfront promenade to get your bearings, feel the warm Aegean breeze, and soak in your first full Greek morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the nearest local beach (steps from the resort). Swim in the warm Aegean Sea, sunbathe, and relax. Rent a sun lounger and umbrella for the afternoon. Explore the shoreline on foot.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll into the nearest village or harbor area for your first proper Greek dinner. Explore the waterfront tavernas and pick one that looks lively with locals.

meals.breakfast: Buffet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort — enjoy Greek yogurt with honey, fresh fruit, and pastries
meals.lunch: Beachside snack bar — try a classic Greek salad, pita with tzatziki, and fresh-squeezed lemonade
meals.dinner: Waterfront taverna — order grilled octopus, horiatiki salad, and a carafe of local white wine (budget ~€25–35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Stay hydrated — the June sun is intense. Apply sunscreen regularly. This is a recovery and orientation day, so keep the pace relaxed.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the local morning market (laiki agora) to experience authentic Greek daily life. Browse stalls selling fresh produce, olives, local cheeses, herbs, and honey. Chat with vendors and pick up snacks for the day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a short boat trip or water taxi to a nearby secluded cove or small island beach accessible from your resort area. Snorkel in the crystal-clear water and explore the rocky coastline.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area and enjoy a sunset cocktail at a cliffside or beachfront bar. Watch the famous Greek golden hour before heading to dinner.

meals.breakfast: Local bakery near the market — spanakopita (spinach pie), tiropita (cheese pie), and Greek coffee
meals.lunch: Packed picnic from market finds — olives, local cheese, bread, tomatoes, and fruit enjoyed on the boat or cove beach
meals.dinner: Traditional psarotaverna (fish taverna) — fresh catch of the day, grilled whole fish, and tzatziki with pita (budget ~€25–35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Check boat trip schedules and book in advance at the hotel concierge. Bring snorkeling gear if you have it, or rent locally. Wear water shoes for rocky coves.

day_by_day.morning: Explore a nearby ancient archaeological site or hilltop village within easy reach of the resort. Visit the local church or Byzantine chapel and learn about the area's history with a self-guided walk.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the beach for a long afternoon swim session. Try paddleboarding or kayaking rented from the resort beach. Explore the coastline by water at your own pace.
day_by_day.evening: Join a local cooking class or food tour in the village (book through the hotel concierge). Learn to make traditional Greek dishes like moussaka, dolmades, or baklava.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — eggs, feta cheese, olives, and fresh bread with local honey
meals.lunch: Casual mezze lunch at a village kafeneion (traditional café) — shared plates of dips, grilled vegetables, and bread
meals.dinner: Enjoy the fruits of your cooking class or dine at a recommended local family-run taverna — try lamb kleftiko or stuffed peppers (budget ~€20–30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Cooking classes typically run 2–3 hours in the evening and cost €50–80 per person. Book 1–2 days ahead. Great way to bring home authentic Greek recipes.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early morning walk along the beach before the crowds arrive. Collect sea glass, watch local fishermen bring in their catch, and enjoy the peaceful golden light. Optional: join a sunrise yoga session if the resort offers one.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby town or port for shopping and sightseeing. Browse local shops for handmade ceramics, olive oil products, natural sponges, and Greek herbs. Visit a local museum or cultural center if available.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a relaxed beach dinner or rooftop dining experience. Enjoy the warm evening air and stargazing over the Aegean.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast — Greek yogurt, honey, walnuts, and a strong Greek coffee at a beachside café
meals.lunch: Souvlaki wrap or gyros from a local street food spot in town — authentic and budget-friendly (€5–8 per person)
meals.dinner: Resort restaurant or a highly rated local taverna — try lamb chops, village sausages, and a Greek salad with a glass of Assyrtiko white wine (budget ~€30–40 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Shops in Greece often close midday (2–5 PM) for siesta, so plan shopping for morning or late afternoon. Bargaining is not common in most shops.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day excursion: depart early for a boat tour along the coastline or to nearby islands. Most tours include multiple swimming stops at hidden bays and sea caves with stunning turquoise water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the boat tour — enjoy on-board lunch, swimming, and snorkeling at designated stops. Relax on the deck and take in the dramatic Greek island scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by late afternoon. Freshen up and enjoy a quiet evening walk through the local village. Find a small taverna tucked off the main tourist strip for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at the resort before departure — bread, cheese, fruit, and coffee
meals.lunch: On-board boat tour lunch — typically included or available for purchase: sandwiches, fruit, and drinks
meals.dinner: Off-the-beaten-path village taverna — try dakos (Cretan rusk salad), grilled calamari, and local raki or ouzo (budget ~€20–28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Boat tours typically cost €40–70 per person. Book through the hotel or a local agency. Bring sunscreen, a hat, a light cover-up, and motion sickness tablets if needed.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recharge day. Sleep in, enjoy a long resort breakfast, and spend the morning by the pool or on the beach with a good book. This is your mid-trip recovery day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the resort's amenities — spa treatment, beach volleyball, or a gentle swim. Alternatively, rent a bicycle and cycle along the coastal road to a nearby beach or viewpoint.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset dinner at the most scenic restaurant you can find nearby — ideally with a terrace overlooking the sea. Celebrate the halfway point of your trip.

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast — take your time, try everything on offer
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the resort beach bar — grilled halloumi, fresh salad, and a cold Mythos or Alfa beer
meals.dinner: Upscale-casual seafood restaurant with sea views — try fresh prawns, sea bream, and a shared mezze platter. Splurge slightly tonight (budget ~€40–55 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Day 7 is intentionally slower-paced. Greece is best enjoyed without rushing — embrace the Greek concept of 'siga siga' (slowly, slowly). Recharge for the second half of the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Take a guided hiking or walking tour of the local area — coastal trails, olive groves, or a nearby gorge or nature reserve. Enjoy the landscape and wildflowers with a knowledgeable local guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a traditional Greek winery or olive oil producer in the region for a tasting experience. Learn about local agricultural traditions and sample regional products.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area and enjoy a mezze evening — order multiple small plates and share them over a long, leisurely dinner in true Greek style.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before the hike — eggs, bread, and strong coffee
meals.lunch: Post-hike lunch at a rural taverna or farmhouse restaurant — try slow-cooked stifado (beef stew) or roasted lamb with village potatoes
meals.dinner: Mezze dinner at a lively local restaurant — order htipiti (spicy feta dip), grilled mushrooms, dolmades, and saganaki (fried cheese) to share (budget ~€22–30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Hiking tours typically cost €20–40 per person. Wear comfortable closed-toe shoes and bring plenty of water. Winery tastings usually cost €10–20 per person and include 4–6 wines.

day_by_day.morning: Beach morning at a different stretch of coastline — take a short drive or water taxi to a beach known for its clear water and quieter atmosphere. Arrive early to claim a good spot.
day_by_day.afternoon: Try a water sport you haven't done yet — windsurfing, jet skiing, or parasailing if available in the area. Many Greek beaches offer rentals and lessons for beginners.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the local harbor or port area for the traditional Greek evening stroll (volta). Join locals promenading along the waterfront before settling in for a late dinner.

meals.breakfast: Grab-and-go from a local bakery — koulouri (sesame bread ring), a cheese pie, and Greek iced coffee (freddo espresso)
meals.lunch: Beach taverna at the new beach — grilled fish, Greek salad, and cold beer or fresh juice
meals.dinner: Harbor-side restaurant — try whole grilled fish sold by weight, accompanied by horta (wild greens) and lemon potatoes (budget ~€28–38 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Water sports prices vary: jet ski ~€30–50 for 30 min, parasailing ~€40–60. Always use licensed operators. Ask your hotel for recommended beaches that require transport.

day_by_day.morning: Cultural morning: visit a local Byzantine church, archaeological museum, or historical monument in the nearest town. Take time to understand the layered history of the region — ancient, Byzantine, and Ottoman influences.
day_by_day.afternoon: Relax at the resort pool or beach. Read, nap, or simply float in the Aegean. Enjoy the warmth of the afternoon sun without any agenda.
day_by_day.evening: Street food and night market exploration — wander through a local evening market or festival if one is running. Sample loukoumades (Greek honey donuts), grilled corn, and local sweets.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast with a focus on local specialties — ask for local honey, regional cheeses, and seasonal fruit
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch — club sandwich, fresh fruit platter, and a smoothie or cold drink at the resort
meals.dinner: Night market street food or a casual souvlaki restaurant — mix of grilled meats, pita wraps, and local pastries for dessert (budget ~€12–18 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Check with your hotel about any local festivals or events happening this evening — June often has cultural celebrations and outdoor concerts in Greek villages.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning snorkeling excursion to a marine-rich area or underwater cave accessible from the resort area. Many local operators offer guided snorkeling trips to see sea turtles, starfish, and colorful fish.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local artisan workshop — pottery, weaving, or jewelry making. Watch craftspeople at work and purchase a handmade souvenir directly from the maker.
day_by_day.evening: Rooftop or terrace dinner with panoramic views. Choose a restaurant elevated above the village or coastline for a memorable dining experience with the best views of the trip.

meals.breakfast: Light pre-excursion breakfast — fruit, yogurt, and coffee at the resort
meals.lunch: Post-snorkeling mezze at a seaside café — taramasalata, grilled bread, olives, and fresh lemonade
meals.dinner: Rooftop restaurant — try slow-roasted lamb, grilled vegetables, and a regional red wine like Xinomavro or Agiorgitiko (budget ~€35–45 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Snorkeling excursions cost ~€25–45 per person. Book the evening restaurant in advance as rooftop spots fill up quickly. This is a great night for photos — bring your camera.

day_by_day.morning: Final full beach day — return to your favorite beach of the trip. Swim, sunbathe, and take it all in one last time. Reflect on the highlights of the journey.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute souvenir shopping in the village — pick up local olive oil, thyme honey, dried herbs, Greek coffee, or handmade crafts for friends and family back home.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at the best restaurant you've discovered during the trip — revisit a favorite or try somewhere new that's been recommended. Make it a celebration.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast — enjoy every bite of the Greek yogurt, pastries, and fresh fruit
meals.lunch: Classic gyros or souvlaki at your favorite local spot — a proper Greek farewell lunch
meals.dinner: Celebratory farewell dinner — order generously: seafood platter, lamb, multiple mezze, local wine, and finish with loukoumades or galaktoboureko (custard pastry) for dessert (budget ~€40–55 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Pack non-breakable souvenirs in checked luggage. Wrap fragile items like olive oil bottles carefully. Begin packing tonight if your departure is early tomorrow.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — wake up early for one last sunrise walk on the beach. Take photos, collect a small stone or shell as a memento, and say goodbye to the Aegean. Check out of the resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure time: transfer to the airport or port. Allow ample time for check-in and security. Enjoy a final Greek coffee at the airport.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Greece with wonderful memories, a sun-kissed glow, and a suitcase full of local flavors and souvenirs.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the resort or a nearby café before checkout — coffee, pastry, and fresh juice
meals.lunch: Airport or departure terminal — grab a final Greek snack: a cheese pie, olives, or a freddo cappuccino
meals.dinner: In-flight or at home — dream about your next Greek adventure

day_by_day.notes: Check out time is typically 11 AM — confirm with the resort. Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for airport check-in and security. Keep travel documents, valuables, and snacks in your carry-on.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Greece Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Navagio Beach (Shipwreck Beach) Visit
experiences.description: Take a boat tour to the iconic Navagio Beach on Zakynthos, one of Greece's most photographed beaches. The stunning turquoise waters, white sand, and the famous shipwreck make this an unmissable experience. Boat tours depart regularly from Porto Vromi or Zakynthos Town.

experiences.name: Athens Central Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the vibrant Varvakios Agora (Athens Central Market) and surrounding streets in Monastiraki. Sample local cheeses, olives, cured meats, fresh seafood, and traditional Greek street food like souvlaki and spanakopita. Engage with local vendors and discover authentic Greek flavors.

experiences.name: Elafonissi Pink Sand Beach Day
experiences.description: Visit the breathtaking Elafonissi Beach, famous for its unique pinkish sand created by crushed shells and coral. Wade through shallow crystal-clear lagoons and snorkel in the warm Mediterranean waters. The beach is part of a protected nature reserve and is one of Crete's most beautiful natural wonders.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Athens International Airport at 22:30 on flight UA. A private luxury transfer will be waiting to whisk you to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, unwind with a welcome drink at the resort bar, and settle into your beachfront suite.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable
meals.lunch: Not applicable
meals.dinner: Light late-night room service at the resort — enjoy a curated cheese and charcuterie board with local Greek wines from the in-room menu

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange private airport transfer with the resort concierge before departure. Request a late check-in amenity tray to be placed in your suite. Keep the first night low-key to recover from travel.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely start to your Greek adventure. Take a slow morning stroll along the resort's private beachfront, dipping your toes into the warm Aegean Sea. Explore the resort grounds and arrange your itinerary details with the concierge.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon lounging on the resort's private beach. Rent a luxury sun cabana, swim in the crystal-clear warm waters, and enjoy water sports such as paddleboarding or snorkeling arranged through the resort. The sea temperature in June is perfect for extended swimming.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a sunset cocktail at the resort's cliffside or beachfront bar, watching the famous Greek golden hour light up the Aegean. Dine at the resort's signature fine-dining restaurant for a refined introduction to Greek cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Indulgent Greek breakfast spread at the resort restaurant — fresh-baked koulouri, local thyme honey, Cretan graviera cheese, strained yogurt with seasonal fruit, and freshly squeezed orange juice
meals.lunch: Beachside lunch at the resort's beach club — grilled octopus, fresh seafood mezze platter, and chilled Assyrtiko white wine
meals.dinner: Resort signature restaurant — slow-roasted lamb kleftiko, saffron-infused orzo, and a selection from their curated Greek wine cellar. Finish with loukoumades drizzled with Aegean thyme honey

day_by_day.notes: This is your orientation day. Use the concierge to confirm all upcoming excursion bookings. Apply high-SPF sunscreen — the June sun at 29°C is intense, especially on the water.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early for the Athens Central Market Food Tour — explore the iconic Varvakios Agora (Athens Central Market) and the vibrant surrounding streets of Monastiraki. Walk through stalls overflowing with fresh fish, hanging cured meats, barrels of olives, and fragrant spices. A private guide will narrate the cultural and culinary history of each section.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue through Monastiraki's food streets, sampling street food including spanakopita, loukoumades, and freshly grilled souvlaki. Browse artisan food shops for premium Greek products — extra-virgin olive oils, aged cheeses, and wild herbs. Visit a traditional taverna for a sit-down meze lunch before returning to the resort.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort and unwind with a sunset swim from the private beach. Dine at a nearby acclaimed local restaurant recommended by the concierge, focusing on hyper-local seasonal ingredients.

meals.breakfast: At the resort before departing — Greek yogurt parfait, honey-drizzled pastries, and strong Greek coffee (ellinikos kafes)
meals.lunch: Traditional taverna in Monastiraki during the food tour — a full spread of mezedes including taramasalata, dolmades, grilled halloumi, and fresh bread with olive oil
meals.dinner: Upscale local restaurant near the resort — whole grilled sea bream caught that morning, lemon-herb roasted potatoes, and a bottle of Santorini Assyrtiko

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes for the market tour — cobblestones and busy market floors can be uneven. Bring a small insulated bag or ask your guide to arrange packaging if you wish to purchase artisan food products to take home.

day_by_day.morning: Book a private luxury sailing charter departing from the nearest marina. Sail along the stunning coastline, stopping at secluded coves and sea caves accessible only by boat. Snorkel in gin-clear turquoise waters and enjoy the privacy of a chartered vessel with a dedicated crew.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the sailing charter with a leisurely anchor at a hidden bay for swimming and sunbathing on the deck. The crew will serve a fresh onboard lunch. Return to the marina by late afternoon and transfer back to the resort.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxing evening at the resort's spa — book a traditional Greek olive oil and honey massage or a sea salt scrub treatment. Dine alfresco at the resort terrace under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast — eggs prepared to order, smoked salmon, fresh-squeezed juices, and a selection of Greek pastries
meals.lunch: Onboard the sailing charter — a lavish spread of fresh seafood, local cheeses, chilled melon, crusty bread, and chilled rosé wine prepared by the boat's crew
meals.dinner: Resort terrace alfresco dining — grilled lobster with herb butter, village salad with barrel-aged feta, and a chilled Greek white wine flight

day_by_day.notes: Book the private sailing charter at least 48 hours in advance through the concierge. Apply waterproof sunscreen generously — sun reflection off the water intensifies UV exposure significantly.

day_by_day.morning: Take a private guided tour of a nearby ancient archaeological site or historic village. Explore well-preserved ruins, Byzantine churches, or a traditional hilltop village (chora) with a knowledgeable local historian guide who can bring the stories to life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local family-run olive grove and winery for an exclusive private tasting experience. Tour the olive press, learn about centuries-old olive cultivation traditions, and taste premium extra-virgin olive oils paired with artisan breads. Follow with a wine tasting of indigenous Greek varietals.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a private in-suite dinner experience — arrange with the concierge for a private chef to prepare a bespoke Greek feast on your terrace overlooking the sea.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the resort — fresh fruit platter, Greek yogurt, and a double espresso
meals.lunch: At the olive grove and winery — a rustic farm-to-table lunch featuring homemade dips, fresh vegetables, local cheeses, and bread baked in a traditional wood-fired oven
meals.dinner: Private in-suite chef experience on your beachfront terrace — five-course tasting menu featuring the best of Greek ingredients: sea urchin bruschetta, prawn saganaki, lamb chops with tzatziki, and baklava semifreddo

day_by_day.notes: Confirm the private chef dinner experience with the concierge at least 24 hours ahead. The olive grove visit is best in the morning light but has been scheduled for the afternoon — confirm exact timings locally as some estates have set tour hours.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a slow, indulgent morning at the resort. Take an early swim in the warm Aegean, then enjoy a long breakfast. Spend time reading or relaxing in your beachfront suite before heading out.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a private speedboat transfer or chartered flight to Zakynthos for the Navagio Beach (Shipwreck Beach) Visit. Arrive by private boat tour to the iconic Navagio Beach — one of Greece's most photographed and dramatic beaches, enclosed by towering white limestone cliffs with the famous shipwreck of the MV Panagiotis resting on the shore.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the cliffs above Navagio at sunset for breathtaking panoramic views. Return by boat and either stay overnight in Zakynthos at a luxury property or return to the main resort via private transfer.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely resort breakfast — full Greek spread with freshly baked tiropita, cold cuts, and honey
meals.lunch: Packed luxury picnic prepared by the resort chef — enjoyed on the boat or on the beach at Navagio: prosciutto wraps, local cheese, fresh fruit, and chilled sparkling wine
meals.dinner: Upscale seafood taverna in Zakynthos town or port — fresh grilled fish of the day, garlic shrimp, and local Zakynthian wines

day_by_day.notes: Navagio Beach is only accessible by boat — the private boat tour is essential. The beach can get crowded midday; arriving by private charter allows for early access. Wear water shoes as the beach is pebbly. If staying overnight in Zakynthos, arrange luxury accommodation in advance.

day_by_day.morning: If overnight in Zakynthos: explore the island's interior — visit the historic Venetian Castle of Zakynthos overlooking the town, and stroll through the charming main square. If returned to main resort: enjoy a peaceful morning yoga session on the beach at sunrise, followed by a refreshing swim.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Aegean Bliss Resort if not already there. Spend the afternoon at the resort's infinity pool or private beach, enjoying the peak of the summer solstice sunshine. Arrange a private cocktail mixing class at the resort bar — learn to craft classic Greek cocktails using local spirits like mastiha and tsipouro.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate the summer solstice with a special dinner. Many Greek resorts and restaurants host special events on this night — check with the concierge for any local celebrations, outdoor concerts, or cultural performances.

meals.breakfast: If in Zakynthos: local kafeneion breakfast — fresh koulouri, local honey, and strong Greek coffee. If at resort: full resort breakfast spread
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch at the resort — mezze sharing platter, fresh watermelon, and chilled rosé
meals.dinner: Special summer solstice dinner at the resort's premium restaurant or a nearby acclaimed taverna — grilled whole fish, seasonal vegetables, and a celebratory bottle of Greek sparkling wine (Amalia Brut)

day_by_day.notes: June 21st is the summer solstice — the longest day of the year. Sunset will be very late (around 9 PM), offering a spectacular extended golden hour. This is a perfect evening for outdoor dining.

day_by_day.morning: Arrange a private guided sea kayaking or stand-up paddleboarding excursion along the coastline near the resort. Explore hidden sea caves, arch formations, and secluded beaches accessible only from the water. A guide will accompany you for safety and local knowledge.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby traditional fishing village for an authentic local experience. Walk the waterfront, browse small artisan shops, and watch local fishermen bring in their afternoon catch. Purchase fresh fish directly from the boats if available.
day_by_day.evening: Cooking class experience — join a private Greek cooking class hosted by a local chef or at the resort. Learn to prepare traditional dishes such as moussaka, spanakopita, and fresh tzatziki from scratch using locally sourced ingredients.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast before kayaking — fresh fruit, energy bar, and Greek coffee
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood lunch at a waterfront taverna in the fishing village — grilled calamari, prawn pasta, and a carafe of chilled local white wine
meals.dinner: Enjoy the dishes you prepared during the cooking class — dine together with your instructor in a convivial, relaxed setting with local wine pairings

day_by_day.notes: Book the sea kayaking excursion through the concierge and confirm fitness requirements. The cooking class is best booked 2–3 days in advance — ask the concierge for the highest-rated local option or an in-resort experience.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early for the Elafonissi Pink Sand Beach Day — travel to the breathtaking Elafonissi Beach (if geographically accessible from your base, or arrange a domestic flight/private transfer to Crete). Famous for its unique pinkish sand created by crushed coral and shells, this UNESCO-protected lagoon is one of Greece's most magical beaches.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the full afternoon at Elafonissi — wade through the shallow turquoise lagoon, explore the pink sand dunes, and swim in the warm, calm waters. The lagoon is only knee-deep in places, making it idyllic for leisurely wading. Rent a private beach setup with sun loungers and umbrella.
day_by_day.evening: Return journey to the resort. Enjoy a quiet evening in — room service or a relaxed dinner at the resort after a full day of sun and travel.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast to go — packed pastries, fruit, and coffee for the journey
meals.lunch: Packed luxury picnic from the resort or a beachside snack bar near Elafonissi — fresh sandwiches, local olives, cheese, and cold drinks
meals.dinner: Relaxed resort dinner — light Mediterranean sharing plates, fresh salads, and chilled white wine. Opt for the resort's lighter menu after a full day outdoors

day_by_day.notes: Elafonissi is located on the southwestern tip of Crete — confirm travel logistics carefully with the concierge. If your base resort is not in Crete, a domestic flight or fast ferry may be required. Arrive early to secure the best spot, as this beach is popular even in the shoulder season. Wear reef-safe sunscreen to protect the ecosystem.

day_by_day.morning: Full spa morning at Aegean Bliss Resort — indulge in a series of treatments including a thalassotherapy seawater bath, a Greek volcanic stone massage, and a hydrating facial using local mastiha and olive extracts. This is a well-deserved recovery day after yesterday's travel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private beach afternoon — reserve a luxury cabana on the resort's private beach. Enjoy complimentary chilled towels, fresh fruit skewers, and personalized cocktail service. Read, swim, and simply soak in the stunning surroundings.
day_by_day.evening: Visit a rooftop bar or cliffside cocktail lounge nearby for sundowner drinks with panoramic Aegean views. Return to the resort for a premium dinner experience.

meals.breakfast: In-suite breakfast delivered to your terrace — eggs Benedict with smoked salmon, fresh-pressed juices, and a pot of Greek mountain tea
meals.lunch: Beachside cabana service — light mezze, fresh fruit, and chilled sparkling water with cucumber and mint
meals.dinner: Resort's premium restaurant — slow-braised beef with kritharaki pasta, roasted seasonal vegetables, and a full Greek wine pairing menu selected by the sommelier

day_by_day.notes: Book spa treatments at least 24 hours in advance — June is peak season and slots fill quickly. This is intentionally a rest-focused day to recharge before the final days of the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Take a private guided food and culture walk through a nearby traditional Greek town or village market. Visit the local laiki agora (weekly street market) for fresh produce, local cheeses, honey, and handmade products. Engage with vendors and learn about seasonal Greek ingredients.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a renowned local restaurant or taverna for a long, leisurely Greek lunch — the Mediterranean tradition of a multi-hour midday meal. Order extensively from the menu and pair with a selection of local wines. Explore the town on foot afterward before returning to the resort.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset boat cruise — arrange a private small-group or couples sunset cruise departing from the local marina. Sail along the coast as the sun dips below the horizon, sipping champagne and enjoying canapés on deck.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — full spread with a focus on local specialties: Cretan dakos rusk with tomato and feta, fresh honey, and strong coffee
meals.lunch: Long traditional Greek lunch at a celebrated local taverna — begin with a full mezze spread, move to a main of slow-cooked goat stifado, and finish with galaktoboureko (custard pastry) and Greek brandy
meals.dinner: Light onboard canapés during the sunset cruise — smoked fish bites, mini spanakopita, and chilled Champagne or Prosecco. Return for a light late snack at the resort bar

day_by_day.notes: The long Greek lunch is a cultural institution — embrace the pace and plan for 2–3 hours at the table. Confirm the sunset cruise departure time with the marina as it will shift slightly each day; June 25th sunset is approximately 8:45 PM.

day_by_day.morning: Final full beach morning — wake early for a sunrise swim in the Aegean. The sea at this hour is calm and mirror-like. Enjoy one last long breakfast on the resort terrace, savoring every detail of your surroundings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a nearby artisan shop or boutique for premium Greek souvenirs — hand-painted ceramics, gold jewelry inspired by ancient designs, premium olive oil sets, local honey, and aged cheeses. Visit a local apiary or artisan producer if available for a behind-the-scenes experience.
day_by_day.evening: Grand farewell dinner — reserve the resort's best table or book a celebrated fine-dining restaurant nearby for your final evening. Make it a special occasion with a tasting menu and full wine pairing.

meals.breakfast: Celebratory final full breakfast at the resort — order everything you loved throughout the trip: yogurt, honey, fresh pastries, eggs, local cheeses, and a glass of fresh orange juice
meals.lunch: Casual beachside lunch — grilled fish, Greek salad, and chilled white wine with your feet in the sand
meals.dinner: Farewell fine-dining experience — seven-course tasting menu featuring the finest Greek ingredients: sea urchin, langoustine, aged feta, Wagyu-style Greek beef, and a grand dessert platter. Pair with a full Greek wine flight curated by the sommelier

day_by_day.notes: Book the farewell dinner well in advance — the best tables at premium restaurants in peak June season fill up quickly. Consider requesting a special setup (rose petals, champagne on arrival, personalized menu) to mark the occasion.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — wake for one last sunrise swim or a quiet walk along the beach. Pack and prepare for departure. Enjoy a leisurely last breakfast at the resort, soaking in the views of the Aegean one final time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Depending on your departure flight time, arrange a private luxury transfer to the airport. If time allows, stop at a local café or bakery near the airport for a final Greek coffee and pastry.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Greece with extraordinary memories, a suitcase of artisan Greek products, and a deep appreciation for the country's beaches, food, and culture.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast — keep it simple and meaningful: Greek yogurt with thyme honey, fresh fruit, and a perfect cup of ellinikos kafes enjoyed on your terrace
meals.lunch: Light airport lounge meal or a quick stop at a quality café near the airport — a final souvlaki wrap or tiropita and a cold frappe coffee
meals.dinner: Onboard or at destination

day_by_day.notes: Confirm checkout time with the resort and arrange luggage storage if your flight is in the evening. Allow extra time at the airport during peak summer season — Athens International Airport can be busy in June. Ask the resort to prepare a farewell gift bag with local products as a memento.
